A 63-year-old man presents with severe substernal chest pressure, diaphoresis, and ST-segment elevations in the inferior leads. Which management step is most appropriate?
(A) Schedule an outpatient stress test
(B) Immediate percutaneous coronary intervention
(C) Treat with inhaled bronchodilators
(D) Start oral antibiotics for otitis media
(E) Provide reassurance only

A 55-year-old smoker develops crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw. Serum troponin is elevated several hours later. Which diagnosis best explains this presentation?
(A) Gastroesophageal reflux disease
(B) Acute otitis media
(C) Acute myocardial infarction
(D) Asthma exacerbation
(E) Tension headache

A 22-year-old woman with episodic wheezing and chest tightness improves after using a short-acting beta agonist. Which treatment provides the fastest symptom relief?
(A) Inhaled albuterol
(B) Immediate coronary angiography
(C) Tympanostomy tube placement
(D) Proton pump inhibitor therapy
(E) High-dose aspirin only

A 4-year-old child has fever, ear pain, and a bulging erythematous tympanic membrane after an upper respiratory infection. What is the most likely diagnosis?
(A) Myocardial infarction
(B) Asthma exacerbation
(C) Gastroesophageal reflux disease
(D) Acute otitis media
(E) Pulmonary embolism
